bug_description.normalized: The staged 128-byte witness makes `compress_fuzzer` select `blosclz`, call `blosc_set_blocksize(4096)`, and call `blosc_set_splitmode(BLOSC_ALWAYS_SPLIT)` before invoking `blosc_compress()` with `nbytes = 128` and `destsize = 128` on a 129-byte heap allocation from `malloc(size + 1)`. `blosc_compress()` forwards that global configuration into `initialize_context_compression()`, which stores a 128-byte source, a 128-byte destination budget, and `compcode = BLOSC_BLOSCLZ`; `compute_blocksize()` then ends with a single 128-byte block. `write_compression_header()` reserves 20 bytes, `serial_blosc()` forwards `ntbytes = 20` and `dest + 20` into `blosc_c()`, and `blosc_c()` reserves one more 4-byte split-length slot before clipping the `blosclz` output budget to `maxout = 104` at overall output offset 24. In `blosclz_compress()`, the encoder writes its initial 5-byte literal prologue before defining `op_limit`, so `op_limit` is based on `output + 5` instead of the slice base. All later bounds checks are therefore 5 bytes too permissive. On the saved crashing run, the leftover-literal guard at `blosclz.c:587` still passes after `op` has crossed the real 104-byte slice, and the next `*op++ = *ip++` at line 588 performs the 1-byte heap overflow that ASAN reports at `0x60d0000000c1`.

source.description: First project-code state creation on the vulnerable path. The library stores the witness-selected compressor code in global state, and later `blosc_compress()` uses that state to dispatch into the `BLOSC_BLOSCLZ` encoder that contains the bug.
source.value_from: The staged 128-byte `poc` has sha256 `891125cfc53e05e4f724b46740f39816cff8dea7f6a4af4c9903ef0c94ac70b3` and begins with bytes `c5 09 00 00 00`. In `tests/fuzz/fuzz_compress.c`, `data[2] = 0` makes `compressors[cindex % 6]` equal `"blosclz"`, so `blosc_set_compressor("blosclz")` stores `code = BLOSC_BLOSCLZ` at line 2004. The same witness then makes `data[3] = 0` trigger `blosc_set_blocksize(4096)` and `data[4] = 0` trigger `blosc_set_splitmode(BLOSC_ALWAYS_SPLIT)`. The harness allocates `output = malloc(size + 1)` at line 40 and calls `blosc_compress(level, filter, 1, size, data, output, size)` at line 44 with `size = 128`, so project code later sees a 128-byte source and a 128-byte advertised destination budget even though the heap allocation is 129 bytes.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.code: result = initialize_context_compression(g_global_context, clevel, doshuffle, typesize, nbytes, src, dest, destsize, g_compressor, g_force_blocksize, g_threads);
tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant state is the combination of the witness-selected global compressor settings (`g_compressor = BLOSC_BLOSCLZ`, `g_force_blocksize = 4096`, `g_splitmode = BLOSC_ALWAYS_SPLIT`) and the current `blosc_compress()` call's `nbytes = 128` and `destsize = 128`. `initialize_context_compression()` turns that state into the context that later yields the 104-byte `blosclz` slice and the misbased `op_limit`.

sink.description: ASAN crash site. The leftover-literal path writes one more byte through `op` after the inflated `op_limit` failed to stop the encoder, so the byte store lands just past the heap allocation returned by `malloc(size + 1)` in the harness.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `WRITE of size 1` at `0x60d0000000c1`, 0 bytes to the right of the 129-byte region `[0x60d000000040,0x60d0000000c1)`.

root_cause.description: The encoder defines its output limit after the 5-byte literal prologue has already advanced `op`. As a result, every later bound check treats the end of the writable slice as 5 bytes farther away than the caller actually reserved.
root_cause.note: The fix in `patch.diff` moves this line above the initial `*op++` prologue, confirming that the missing obligation is to anchor `op_limit` at the start of the `blosclz` output slice rather than at the already-advanced cursor.

parser_admitted.description: The witnessed call arrives with `length = 128` and `maxout = 104`, so the early size gate is not taken and execution continues into the buggy prologue/limit sequence.

fine_trace.note: Witness byte `data[2] = 0` makes the harness call `blosc_set_compressor("blosclz")`, and project code stores `g_compressor = BLOSC_BLOSCLZ` as the compressor dispatch key for the upcoming compression call.
Witness byte `data[3] = 0` satisfies the harness guard `data[3] % 7 == 0`, so project code stores the forced blocksize `4096` in `g_force_blocksize`.

depends_on.via: successful compressor selection lets the harness continue past the `i == 6` early return

fine_trace.note: Witness byte `data[4] = 0` makes the harness call `blosc_set_splitmode(BLOSC_ALWAYS_SPLIT)`, and project code stores `g_splitmode = 1` so later split decisions stay on the always-split path.

depends_on.via: successful compressor selection lets the harness reach the later split-mode setter

fine_trace.code: result = initialize_context_compression(g_global_context, clevel, doshuffle, typesize, nbytes, src, dest, destsize, g_compressor, g_force_blocksize, g_threads);
fine_trace.note: On the crashing path, `blosc_compress()` passes the current call's `nbytes = 128`, `destsize = 128`, and `typesize = 1` together with the previously stored `g_compressor = BLOSC_BLOSCLZ` and `g_force_blocksize = 4096` into context initialization.

fine_trace.var: context->src, context->dest, context->destsize, context->sourcesize, context->typesize, context->compcode
fine_trace.code: context->src = (const uint8_t*)src; context->dest = (uint8_t *)(dest); context->destsize = (int32_t)destsize; context->sourcesize = sourcesize; context->typesize = typesize; context->compcode = compressor;
fine_trace.note: The library materializes the compression context from the call arguments: the raw 128-byte input buffer, the destination buffer pointer, the advertised compressed-output budget `128`, `typesize = 1`, and `compcode = BLOSC_BLOSCLZ`.

depends_on.via: src, dest, destsize, nbytes, typesize, g_compressor

fine_trace.code: context->blocksize = compute_blocksize(context, clevel, (int32_t)context->typesize, context->sourcesize, blocksize); context->nblocks = context->sourcesize / context->blocksize; context->leftover = context->sourcesize % context->blocksize; context->nblocks = (context->leftover > 0) ? (context->nblocks + 1) : context->nblocks;
fine_trace.note: The block layout is derived from the witness-controlled configuration. `compute_blocksize()` starts from the forced blocksize `4096`; because step 3 stored `g_splitmode = BLOSC_ALWAYS_SPLIT`, `split_block()` returns true and the split-codec minimum raises the candidate blocksize before the clamp at `blosc.c:1053-1055` reduces it to `nbytes = 128`. The resulting layout is `blocksize = 128`, `nblocks = 1`, and `leftover = 0`.
For the single derived block, the fixed Blosc header plus the block-start table consumes 20 bytes before any compressor payload, so `serial_blosc()` will start the block with `ntbytes = 20`.

The same settings keep splitting enabled at the header level. Because `split_block()` sees `g_splitmode = BLOSC_ALWAYS_SPLIT`, it returns true and `write_compression_header()` stores `dont_split = 0`, so the later `blosclz` call receives `split_block = 1`.

fine_trace.code: int32_t ntbytes = context->num_output_bytes; cbytes = blosc_c(context, bsize, leftoverblock, ntbytes, context->destsize, context->src+j*context->blocksize, context->dest+ntbytes, tmp, tmp2);
fine_trace.note: The missing local handoff happens here. `serial_blosc()` initializes `ntbytes` from step 7's `context->num_output_bytes = 20` and calls `blosc_c()` for the first block with `maxbytes = context->destsize = 128` and `dest = context->dest + 20`.

fine_trace.code: dest += sizeof(int32_t); ntbytes += (int32_t)sizeof(int32_t); maxout = neblock; if (ntbytes+maxout > maxbytes) { maxout = maxbytes - ntbytes; }
fine_trace.note: For this witness, `typesize = 1` keeps `nsplits = 1`, so `neblock = blocksize = 128`. `blosc_c()` reserves one 4-byte split-length slot, moving the payload base from overall output offset 20 to 24, then clips the encoder budget from 128 to `maxout = 104` because `24 + 128 > maxbytes (128)`.

The vulnerable branch is selected because the earlier state made `context->compcode = BLOSC_BLOSCLZ`. Using step 8's `dont_split = 0`, `blosc_c()` calls `blosclz_compress()` with the single 128-byte input block, the payload slice starting at overall output offset 24, `maxout = 104`, and `split_block = 1`.

fine_trace.code: if (length < 16 || maxout < 66) { return 0; } uint8_t copy = 4; *op++ = MAX_COPY - 1; *op++ = *ip++; *op++ = *ip++; *op++ = *ip++; *op++ = *ip++;
fine_trace.note: The size gate passes for `length = 128` and `maxout = 104`. The encoder then writes one literal-control byte plus the first four input bytes, advancing its local output cursor `op` from the start of the `blosclz` slice to `output + 5` before any output limit has been established.

Root cause. Because step 12 already advanced `op` to `output + 5` relative to the `blosclz` slice, this computes `op_limit = output + 109` instead of the intended `output + 104`. Every later `LITERAL` and `MATCH` check is therefore evaluated against a limit that is 5 bytes too high.

fine_trace.code: while (BLOSCLZ_UNLIKELY(ip <= ip_bound)) { if (BLOSCLZ_UNLIKELY(op + 2 > op_limit)) goto out; }
fine_trace.note: This is the last bounds check before each leftover literal byte. By the crashing iteration, omitted normal encoder steps have already advanced the same `op` cursor past the real 104-byte payload slice, but the guard still compares against the inflated `op_limit` from step 13, so it does not jump to `out`.

depends_on.via: same op cursor after intervening encoder writes

fine_trace.note: ASAN sink. The leftover-byte store writes at `0x60d0000000c1`, which the saved trace identifies as the first byte past the 129-byte heap allocation from `malloc(size + 1)` in `tests/fuzz/fuzz_compress.c:40`. The overflow is reachable only because step 14 let execution fall through after step 13 had overstated the writable limit.

allocation_context.note: `output = malloc(size + 1)` allocates the 129-byte heap region that ASAN reports. The harness still passes `destsize = size = 128` to `blosc_compress()` at line 44.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_38313 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/compress_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` in `blosclz_compress`.

format.name: 128-byte raw input for `compress_fuzzer`
format.contract: Exactly the staged 128-byte witness `poc` with sha256 `891125cfc53e05e4f724b46740f39816cff8dea7f6a4af4c9903ef0c94ac70b3`. `compress_fuzzer` interprets the first five bytes `c5 09 00 00 00` as `level = 7`, `filter = BLOSC_NOSHUFFLE`, `compressor = blosclz`, `g_force_blocksize = 4096`, and `g_splitmode = BLOSC_ALWAYS_SPLIT`, then passes the whole 128-byte buffer to `blosc_compress()` with `destsize = 128` while the heap allocation is `malloc(size + 1)` = 129 bytes. In the observed run, c-blosc reserves 20 header bytes, `serial_blosc()` forwards the first block from `dest + 20`, `blosc_c()` clips the writable `blosclz` slice to 104 bytes at overall output offset 24, and the exact remaining 123 witness bytes keep the encoder on the compressing path until the misbased `op_limit` allows the leftover-literal write at `blosc/blosclz.c:588`. The staged artifacts prove this exact witness and path, not a broader class of inputs.
